subject: Re: MAP decision backlog — final mile widening & contingency
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@acme.com>, Jim Rolfe <jim.rolfe@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final mile widening — decision backlog and contingency ask

Sarah / Jim —

Quick update from our side after the MAP review this morning. The evaluation gates look healthy, but the procurement decision backlog on SOW items B and C plus the missing security-deployment appendix will push acceptance beyond the target close date if we do not lock decisions by end of week.

Two concrete asks:
- Can Acme confirm (A) final acceptance criteria for SOW B and (B) whether the deployment appendix will be provided by the 3rd? If not, we need to trigger the contingency timeline.
- If decisions slide past Friday, we propose a contingency "final-mile widening": shift the go-live window by 10 business days and enable an expanded test window (we'll allocate extra validation cycles).

I've attached an updated MAP (redwood_MAP_v3.pdf) and a procurement checklist (procurement_requirements.xlsx) that highlights gating items. If you prefer, we can run a 30-minute decision sync tomorrow to clear open points.

If we do need to widen the window, we want to lock that change now so engineering and procurement can reserve capacity and avoid an expensive overtime surge.

Thanks — appreciate a quick read and a yes/no for the decision sync time.

Best,

Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0183

Attachment: redwood_MAP_v3.pdf (MAP, 3 pages)
Attachment: procurement_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 2 sheets)
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@acme.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jim Rolfe <jim.rolfe@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final mile widening — decision backlog and contingency ask

Thanks Grace.

Short answer: we are still waiting on legal to sign off on the deployment appendix and procurement is validating budget reallocation for SOW B. Both teams said earliest they can finish is EOD Thursday.

We appreciate the contingency proposal — can you enumerate the customer-impact tradeoffs for a 10-business-day shift vs a phased go-live (partial acceptance for core API, defer analytics features)? Procurement would prefer the phased approach to reduce license ramp and budget strain.

I can do a quick sync tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT if that helps.

—Sarah
Sarah Park
Director, Product Ops | Acme Corp
sarah.park@acme.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jim Rolfe <jim.rolfe@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final mile widening — decision backlog and contingency ask

Sarah —

Thanks for the quick note. We agree that a phased go-live is preferable if Acme can accept limited scope at day-1. High-level tradeoffs:

- 10-business-day shift: full scope, single cutover. Pros: single QA matrix, all features validated together, lower coordination overhead. Cons: delayed value capture, potential impact to Q2 metrics, cost for reserved engineering time.
- Phased go-live (core API first): Pros: earlier delivery of critical capabilities, smaller immediate procurement hit, reduced testing surface. Cons: requires more incremental rollout tracking, two acceptance gates (core + analytics), slightly higher total validation hours.

Recommendation: run the phased plan as the default contingency. If legal and procurement confirm EOD Thursday the appendix and SOW funding, we retract the contingency and keep original close date. If not, we execute phased go-live with explicit acceptance criteria we can include in the MAP.

I'll run the 10:00 AM PT sync tomorrow. Laura — can you bring the updated QA acceptance checklist and the proposed phased acceptance language? Jonas — can you confirm estimated incremental validation hours if we go phased (quick number pls)? Ben — I'll need a brief note from you on procurement constraints and whether partial licenses are acceptable.

Grace

Grace / team —

Quick engineering estimate for the phased approach:
- Core API validation (sanity + load): 3 engineer-days (2 infra, 1 QA)
- Analytics feature validation (deferred): 4 engineer-days when scheduled
- Integration cadence: two 2-hour deployment windows for core + final sync

If we need to do the widened single cutover instead, I recommend we budget an additional 2 engineer-days for pre-cutover soak and an extra on-call rotation the week of the cut.

I'll mark the MAP with the phased acceptance language and push a short decision table to the Drive link. Laura, attaching the preliminary acceptance checklist would help the sync.

Jonas

Thanks everyone for the sync and the updated notes. Legal confirmed the deployment appendix and procurement confirmed partial license approval for core API. We will proceed with the phased go-live: core API on the original close date, analytics deferred to the widened window (T+10 business days).

Action items (accepted):
- Grace: update MAP to reflect phased acceptance criteria and publish v4 (redwood_MAP_v4.pdf) to the Drive folder.
- Jonas: lock core API validation window and schedule 2-hour deployment on close date.
- Ben: confirm purchase order for partial license and send PO to procurement@redwood.com by EOD Friday.

We appreciate the contingency framing — having that lined up made the decision clearer.

Best,

—Sarah
